 JUDGMENT
Though these appeals are listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties the same is taken up for final disposal.

2. These two appeals filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) are arising out of common judgment and award dated 16.08.2019 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal No.13, Vijayapur.

sentences.text: 3. MFA No.201223/2021 is filed by claimant- Kareppa in MVC No.490/2015 for the personal injury suffered by him in a motor vehicle accident dated 26.11.2014, whereas MFA No.201245/2021 is filed by claimant-Mallappa in MVC No.489/2015 for the damages caused to the Tractor bearing registration No.KA-48/T-4196 in the said accident.
4. Since these two appeals are arising out of the same judgment and award, they are clubbed together and are decided by a common order.

5. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
6. FACTS: It is the case of the petitioners that on 26.11.2014 at about 12.50 a.m., petitioner-Kareppa was driving Tractor bearing registration No.KA-48/T-4196 ('the Tractor' for short) in a slow and cautious manner from Bagalkot towards Jamakhandi.

Near RTO office at Jamakhandi, a lorry bearing registration No.KA-29-9335 ('the offending vehicle' for short), being driven by its driver in a rash or negligent manner came by opposite side and dashed against the Tractor.
In the said accident, petitioner- Kareppa sustained grievous injuries.
The Tractor was also damaged.
Despite prolonged treatment, petitioner-Kareppa is not completely cured.
He has suffered permanent partial disability.

Petitioner-Mallappa has spent more than Rs.2,80,000/- towards repair of the Tractor and he has suffered loss of Rs.20,000/- for non availability of the Tractor and sought for compensation in a sum of Rs.3,00,000/-.
7.
Before the Tribunal, respondent No.1 has remained exparte.

8. Respondent No.2 filed written statement disputing the age, occupation and income of the petitioner- Kareppa and also the fact that accident was caused due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

It has also denied that in the said accident, the Tractor was extensively damaged and petitioner Mallappa has spent Rs.2,80,000/- for its repair and suffered loss of Rs.20,000/- towards non availability of the Tractor.
Accident was caused due to the rash or negligent driving of the Tractor.
Since the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation and sought for dismissal of the petitions.

3 9.
Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
10. Petitioner-Kareppa has examined himself as PW-1 and petitioner - Mallappa in MVC No.489/2015 is examined as PW-3.
An independent witness is examined as PW-4.
Petitioners have got marked Exs.P-1 to P-26.
11. On the other hand, on behalf of Respondent No.2, RW-1 is examined and Ex.R-1 is marked.

12. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed all the three claim petitions and granted compensation in a sum of Rs.5,09,976/- in favour of petitioner-Kareppa as detailed below:

Heads Amount in Rs.
 Injuries, pain and sufferings 97,000  Medical bill 2,47,226  Loss of income 39,750  Nourishment & Transportation 26,000  Loss of amenities 1,00,000
Based on the survey report, the Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.2,17,000/- in favour of petitioner-Mallappa.
14. Respondent No.2 has not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
15. Petitioner-Kareppa has challenged the impugned judgment and award contending that the compensation granted under all the heads is on the lower side.

No compensation is granted under the head 'loss of future earnings'.
16.

Petitioner-Mallappa has challenged the impugned judgment and award contending that even though he is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.3,00,000/-, the Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.2,17,000/- and it requires interference.
17. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submitted that the compensation granted in both cases is more than what the petitioners deserve and prays to dismiss the appeals.

18. Heard arguments and perused the record.
19.

Considering the fact that petitioner-Kareppa has suffered eight injuries out of which two are simple in nature and also appreciating the testimony of PW-4 Dr.Satish, the Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.97,000/- under the head 'Pain and suffering', Rs.1,00,000/- under the head 'Loss of amenities', Rs.39,750 under the head 'loss of income during laid up period',
Kareppa vs Jagadish And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170559989/
4 Rs.26,000/- under the head 'Nourishment and Transportation' which is substantially on the higher side.
Similarly, based on medical bills, the Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.2,47,226/-.
Looking to the nature of injuries suffered by petitioner-Kareppa, compensation granted is fairly on the higher side.
Absolutely, there are no justifiable grounds to enhance the same.
20. Similarly, the petitioner-Mallappa has produced Survey report for a sum of Rs.2,17,000/-.

Only on the ground that respondent No.2 has not disputed the assessment, the Tribunal has accepted the entire survey report without critically examining each and every item referred to therein and whether actually the petitioner - Mallappa has spent the said amount for repairing the Tractor.
However, respondent No.2 has not challenged the said order.
21. In the circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that in case of petitioner-Mallappa also there are no justifiable grounds to interfere.

22. In the result, both appeal fails and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) Both appeals are dismissed.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is hereby confirmed.
(iii) The Registry is directed to send back the trial Court records along with copy of this judgment to the Tribunal forthwith.
